text:
maya: Quick check — onboarding zeta-rl-13b v2 weights. HF source is https://huggingface.co/rl/zeta-rl-13b-v2, target mirror s3://redwood-artifacts/zeta-rl-13b/v2. Planning a cross-region mirror (eu-west -> us-west). Anyone hit presign TTL expiries for shard pulls across regions?

jon: Yep, saw a bunch of 403s last week during a large shard fetch. Our presign TTL was 60s for per-shard presigns; downloads for big parts sometimes exceed that. We bumped to 15m for one flow — reduced failures. Are you presigning per-part or per-shard?

maya: Presigning per-shard on the replicate job. Mirror job spawns parallel downloads that can be slow if network arbitration happens. I was hoping to keep TTL smaller to reduce exposure, but reliability trumps that for now.

srinath: For replicate jobs I usually set presign TTL = 10m. Also make sure client-side HTTP timeouts > TTL so the SDK doesn't cancel mid-presign. Default streaming client timeout was 60s in our old library.

olga: Heads up — when I ran manifest validation against staging I hit a checksum mismatch on shard_3: manifest lists md5 but S3 ETag was multipart-based. Our validator expects `sha256` in the manifest to avoid ETag ambiguity. artifacts-bot also flagged missing sha256 for that shard.

artifacts-bot: CI | manifest validation failed for zeta-rl-13b/v2: missing field `sha256` for shard_3. See CI logs: https://ci.internal/runs/9981 (auto-note)

maya: OK I can regenerate the manifest with sha256 for each shard. Will also set presign TTL to 12m for the mirror job and increase client timeouts. Re-running mirror now.

jon: FYI when you re-run, set multipart part-size to 50MB for the mirror -> reduces number of parts and ETag confusion. Also add a short retry on 403 to request a fresh presign (race with TTL expiry).

olga: Another tokenizer quirk: the HF tokenizer.json lacks an explicit `pad_token` entry and has `pad_to_max_length: false`. Our serving infra expects `pad_token` present for batched serving codepaths; missing pad token can cause token alignment issues after quantization. Small patch: add "pad_token": "<pad>" and ensure `pad_token_id` matches.

srinath: Good catch. We should also add a quick config lint step in the ingest pipeline that enforces both checksum (sha256) and tokenizer minimal keys (`pad_token`, `pad_token_id`, `model_max_length`). I can open a tiny PR for the linter.

maya: I'll patch the manifest + tokenizer and push a mirror re-run. Pinging @eng-runtime for CI canary and @devex for docs update. CR: https://phabricator/r/CR1234 (patch includes manifest regen + tokenizer.json).

jon: lgtm from infra side. Once mirror reports green checksums, I'll kick a dry-run canary (no traffic) then a canary with 1% traffic.

artifacts-bot: Mirror job 3077801299 started (eu-west -> us-west).

maya: Mirror finished — checksum comparisons passed (sha256 match). Tokenizer patched to include pad_token and pad_token_id. I scheduled canary deploy at 09:30 PST. Thanks for the quick responses :thumbsup:

srinath: Nice. I'll throw the linter PR and add a small test to ensure manifests include sha256 and tokenizer keys.

olga: I'll run the local tokenizer smoke tests against the canary once it's up.

jon: I'll monitor for 403 spikes and presign errors during canary. If anything pops up I'll escalate.

maya: Closing loop here — will update the onboarding checklist with presign TTL guidance and manifest sha256 requirement.
